mappings.note: A poetry circle classed as a community of interest - the item is about what KIND of grouping this is, so LO-191 rather than the institution's role.
Communities depending on one another because each supplies particular goods or services: the socio-economic interdependence of CG-SST4, resting on occupational specialisation (LO-197).
Works out 'Chittappa' as father's younger brother from the South Indian kinship set - family vocabulary, so CG-SST4 with the mausi item.
Rejects halma as individual problem-solving among definitions of joint family, nuclear family and community; all four options concern family and community institutions.
Sorts dana, seva and tyaga by meaning: values transmitted in the family (CG-SST4) that come from India's older traditions (LO-200).
Identifies an apartment association with elected officers and common-area rules as an urban RWA - naming a kind of modern community, so LO-191.
Places Tenzing's family in Meghalaya; the answer is a region (LO-191), reached through a family story (CG-SST4).
Indian languages carrying finer kinship terms than English, and what that says about the value placed on family ties - CG-SST4.
Children learning responsibility through age-appropriate chores; a function of the family as an institution.
Names the Bhils as the community Shivganga worked with: identifying the community (LO-191) and its collective action (CG-SST4).
Defines jati as a caste or sub-caste group - a form of social grouping in the pupil's own society, so LO-191.
Tenzing's grandparents shown as storytellers, tutors and social workers against the stereotype of elderly inactivity - roles within family and community, hence CG-SST4.
Picks the correct definition (ahimsa as non-violence) among dana, seva and tyaga; the same value-vocabulary pair as the other definition items.
Shalini's parents buying clothes for the uncle's family too, putting collective happiness first - the family's internal economy, so CG-SST4.
Rules out 'promoting isolation' from the reasons communities gather; the item is about what a community is FOR, hence CG-SST4.
Assertion that 'community' stretches across religion, region, interest and school clubs - explicitly about the variety of groupings, so LO-191.
Finds the false basis (a school sports team formed on political ideology) among professional, occupational and faith communities; a kinds-of-community item, so LO-191.
Accepts jati, an RWA and a drama club as three valid community types - again the range of groupings, hence LO-191.
Scattered open-source developers counted as a community of common interest despite never meeting; the item extends the community category, so LO-191.
Interdependence alongside love and cooperation in family life - the internal working of the family institution.
Kamal Parmar showing that community service can start with an ordinary person: the contribution of an individual section of society, which CG-SST4 names.
Tenzing's mother joining a handicraft cooperative - a family member's work (CG-SST4) and a rural occupation shaped by local craft and tourism (LO-197).
Weddings and festivals strengthening social bonds and community ties; the binding function of these institutions, so CG-SST4.
Halma's voluntary duty set against funded government relief: the item is a deliberate contrast between a community institution (CG-SST4) and the state's role (LO-194).
Matches each community to its defining basis and settles on the RWA as an urban locality group - a kinds-of-community item, so LO-191.
The family as society's oldest unit; the short-answer twin of the multiple-choice version, under CG-SST4.
Names the joint family as the several-generation household - a form of the family institution.
Names the nuclear family as couple and children; the companion recall to the joint-family item.
Cousins counted as brothers and sisters, showing the closeness of kinship - CG-SST4, as with the other cousin items.
Cooperation as working together within the family; the short-answer form of the definition item.
Names a value learned at home - ahimsa, dana, seva or tyaga: family transmission (CG-SST4) of traditional values (LO-200).
Dana as giving; the one-word recall of the value, mapped like its multiple-choice version.
Seva as service - the companion value to dana, under the same pair of codes.
Onam as the festival Shalini's Kerala family prepares for: a regional festival (LO-191) inside a family story (CG-SST4).
The fabrics and carvings Tenzing's mother makes in the cooperative - the craft occupation itself (LO-197) within the family's life (CG-SST4).
Names a group of connected families and individuals a community; a definition of the grouping, so LO-191.
Gives a reason communities gather - festivals, feasts, weddings, farm work. The community's function, hence CG-SST4.
Names halma as the Bhil practice of rallying round someone in crisis; a community support institution, so CG-SST4.

Places Jhabua, where the Bhils did their water conservation, in Madhya Pradesh - a fact about that community's collective work. Not LO-181, whose States are to be identified on a map rather than recalled from a story.
Mahesh Sharma's Padma Shri for his work with the Bhil communities - recognition of one person's contribution to society, which CG-SST4 covers.
